title: Graduate Engineer Trainee - Mechanical
summary: A graduate engineer trainee (GET) in mechanical joins a factory, public sector plant or EPC company (a firm that designs and builds projects) straight from college. For about a year they rotate through production, maintenance and quality on the shop floor, supporting senior engineers before being confirmed in one department.
dailyDuties: Support shift production and record output on the shop floor
Assist preventive and breakdown maintenance under supervision
Read drawings and check parts with vernier, micrometer and gauges
Prepare or update 2D drawings and 3D models in CAD
Follow PPE and work permit rules and join safety walks
Update daily reports in Excel and attend training sessions

skills.expectation: Make parts and simple assemblies in a CAD tool such as SolidWorks or Creo
Make and edit 2D drawings in AutoCAD
Read part and assembly drawings with tolerances and GD&T symbols
Understand machining, welding, casting and sheet metal processes on the shop floor
Measure parts with vernier, micrometer and gauges
Follow PPE, work permit and lock-out rules on the plant floor
Record production and inspection data and make daily reports
Report shift issues clearly to supervisors and operators
Support preventive and breakdown maintenance under supervision
Join why-why and fishbone analysis of shop-floor problems
Take part in kaizen activities on the line
Help with in-process and final inspection of parts
Run basic stress checks on design changes
Keep records in line with ISO 9001 procedures
Track daily output against the production plan

groups.label: A mechanical CAD tool (3D modelling or AutoCAD 2D)
